extractionNotes: COMPLETE extraction (Phase 9), finished across multiple sessions (Year 1 and part of Year 2 in earlier sessions; Year 2 Waves onward through the end of Year 3 completed in this session by reading the entire remaining source PDF via pdftotext -layout). Final body counts (59 CS / 59 LO / 188 LI) exactly match the document's own Scope-and-Sequence table grand totals (59/59/188) and its per-year breakdown (Year1=18/18/57, Year2=20/20/66, Year3=21/21/65) -- see the per-strand counts reproduced below. No discrepancy to reconcile, unlike some other subjects in this corpus.

SCOPE AND SEQUENCE table (PDF page 21, pdfPageIndex 23 via -f19-l24 read) gives per-sub-strand CS/LO/LI counts per Year. The raw pdftotext -layout extraction visually misaligns the S/N and STRAND-name column against sub-strand rows (Strand names only print on the first sub-strand row of each strand's block, causing the flattened text table to appear to attribute e.g. 'Kinematics' to Strand 2 and 'Dynamics' to Strand 3). This is a text-layout artifact, not the real structure: actual in-body Strand headings (verified while reading Year One) confirm Strand 1 'MECHANICS AND MATTER' covers sub-strands Introduction to Basic Physics, Matter, Kinematics, and Dynamics; Strand 2 'ENERGY' covers Heat and Waves. In-body headings are used as ground truth for strand/sub-strand assignment throughout this file; the scope-and-sequence table is used only to cross-check per-sub-strand CS/LO/LI counts per year, which all matched exactly for Year One strand 1 content (Introduction to Basic Physics 2/2/8, Matter 1/1/2, Kinematics 1/1/3, Dynamics 2/2/6) and Heat (1/1/4). Grand totals per the table: 59 CS / 59 LO / 188 LI overall; Year1=18/18/57, Year2=20/20/66, Year3=21/21/65.

Year 2 and Year 3 body content (completed in the continuation session) carries a high density of source-document numbering typos consistent with the pattern already documented for Year 1: missing separator dots, LI/AS codes printed with an extra '.1' infix (e.g. '2.4.1.LI.1.2' for what should be '2.4.1.LI.2'), wrong sub-strand code prefixes (e.g. a Year 3 Alternating Current Learning Indicator printed as '3.3.1.LI.2' instead of '3.3.2.LI.2'), and at least one severely malformed Content Standard code ('3.1.3.C.S.3.1'). Several Learning Outcome rows are also affected by page-break rendering artifacts -- consecutive duplicate printing (e.g. Year 2 Electromagnetism LO.2, Year 2 Digital Electronics LO.2) or, in one case (Year 2 Electromagnetism LO.3), full character-doubling ('DDeemmoonnssttrraattee' for 'Demonstrate') that required de-duplication to recover the Learning Outcome's description text. All such cases are preserved verbatim in their stored 'code'/'description' fields and flagged NEEDS_REVIEW with a reviewNote explaining the specific anomaly, per this document's established convention; none were silently corrected. Two genuine Learning Indicator code collisions (two distinct LIs sharing one printed code within the same Content Standard) were also found and preserved verbatim: Year 3 Alternating Current CS.2 (both 'LI.3') and Year 3 Nuclear Physics CS.1 (both 'LI.2'), mirroring the collision pattern already documented for Year 1 Atomic/Nuclear Physics ('1.4.2.LI.1.2' printed twice).

Sub-Strand 4 DYNAMICS (Year 1): the document prints TWO Content Standard blocks both effectively coded '1.1.4.CS.1' -- the first as '1.1.4.CS1' (missing the separator dot; covers Newton's laws of motion, LI.1-LI.3, aligned to Learning Outcome 1.1.4.LO.1) and the second as '1.1.4.CS.1' (with the dot; covers pressure, LI.1-LI.3, aligned to Learning Outcome 1.1.4.LO.2). The second should logically be '1.1.4.CS.2' given it is a distinct Content Standard following the first, but is printed identically to the first except for the missing dot in the first occurrence. Preserved exactly as printed in both cases; flagged NEEDS_REVIEW on the second Content Standard object (stored with its printed code '1.1.4.CS.1').

This document places its 'Teaching and Learning Resources' bullet block at the END of each Content Standard's Learning-Indicator list (not once at the end of the whole Sub-Strand, as the canonical schema's illustrative example shows) -- confirmed across every Content Standard block read in Sub-Strands 1-4 of Strand 1 and Sub-Strand 1 (Heat) of Strand 2. To stay faithful to this document's actual structure while remaining compatible with the canonical schema shape, TLR is captured at BOTH levels in this file: a 'teachingLearningResources' array (with 'source_TLR') is stored on each Content Standard object exactly as printed for that CS block, AND the Sub-Strand-level 'teachingLearningResources' array (for canonical-schema compatibility) is the concatenation, in reading order, of all of its Content Standards' TLR items.

teachingLearningResources: Community visits. i.e., universities, industries research institutes.

learningIndicators.description: Identify careers that are related to physics in various sectors of the economy.
pedagogicalExemplars: Collaborative learning: Let learners watch a documentary showing how physics through collaboration and critical thinking plays a vital role in the world. Learners through talk for learning discuss how careers in plumbing, carpentry, welding, vulcanising, masonry is physics oriented careers. Learners discuss physics-oriented careers such as engineering (mechanical, civil, geomatic, electrical), medicine and new areas such as geophysics, materials science, metallurgy, laser physics, radiology, astrophysics, meteorology and climate science and others play vital role in the world. Learners appreciate that success in physics-oriented careers like all others require hard work and resilience. For a physicist, it is important to report observations as seen without personal biases and requires focus.

Grouping be mindful of gender, where applicable. Learners who are not adept in Mathematics and/or in using some digital equipment should be catered. Learners should appreciate that Physics oriented careers are open to everyone.
Provide students with exposure to diverse perspectives and opportunities to engage with professionals who challenge stereotypes and promote inclusive practices in physics.

learningIndicators.description: State Newton's laws of motion.
pedagogicalExemplars: Talk for learning: A vehicle has broken down and as responsible citizens, you know that the vehicle needs to be moved off the road to prevent other cars from crashing into it. Explain using Newton's laws of motion using the following: i. To move the vehicle, the force applied must overcome the inertia of the body (1st Law). ii. The change of speed of the vehicle is dependent on the force being applied (2nd Law). iii. The force applied to the vehicle by those pushing it is equal to the force applied by vehicle on those pushing it (3rd Law).

Learners build simple paper boats and place them in a bowl of water and using made-up paddles, try to move the paper boats. Learners record their observations and using Newton's laws of motion explain the movement of their boats.
Foster an inclusive and respectful classroom culture and address bias in teaching materials and examples.
